correctness.rationale: The unique local two-to-two matching gives a permutation of \(2^k\) states. Its single-cycle condition is equivalent to a de Bruijn word, and the unbordered statistic is exactly the stated weighted sum because uncrossed factors have matching endpoints. A crossing-bit change is one transposition, proving the universal necklace lower/parity constraints. The sixteen weights are computed directly; 65,536 masks and every unique all-zero-anchored cycle are exhaustively counted by independent algorithms. Both give the same 2,048 cycles and 8-value distribution. Exact-rational moments are checked.

value.rationale: Length k+1 is the first factor length not present in full in every order-k de Bruijn cycle. Border-free factor count at this level measures fine motif diversity of a universal cycle. The result supplies a nontrivial all-order crossing-weight and necklace-switch law plus the first richer finite full spectrum at order five: eight attainable values with an internal gap, sharp extrema, exact mean and variance. Neither the classical total cycle count nor the previously recorded palindrome/overlap statistic determines it.
